speaker: nana
lines: There you are. Thinner. The road does that.
Bad timing, love. The radio's gone quiet, and the set up at the mast on Brindle Peak is dead for want of power.
Bram, who keeps the woodstore by the big pine, has spare batteries. And take my old camera: Edda up there has been after one. She'll tell you why.

speaker: nana
lines: Because the snow's early, and when it comes the road closes behind it.
The radio is how the valley checks on itself. Orla's flour, Skiff's ice, whose chimney's gone cold.
Edda keeps the set at the mast. She's sat with a dead box since.
I'd go myself. These knees did that climb sixty winters. They're done.

speaker: nana
lines: He'll want something done first. He always does. Then bring the batteries here.

speaker: nana
lines: Still empty-handed? Don't fret. It's early yet.
Bram keeps the batteries in his woodstore, by the big pine.
He's particular, not mean. Whatever he asks, it'll be quick and it'll be fussy.
Bring them here first, before the hill. There's more you'll need to know.

speaker: nana
lines: You got them off him. Heavy, aren't they? That's the radio's voice in there.
Here. Take my lantern. There are posts all along the trail. Light them as you pass.
Lit, they'll show you the way back down to me.
Edda keeps the set at the mast. Give these to her and nobody else.

speaker: nana
lines: Edda is an owl. Proud, kind, and she can't abide a fuss.
We've talked on that set every evening for thirty years.
She'll ask if I'm well. Tell her yes. She'll pretend she wasn't worried.

speaker: nana
lines: Climb slow. The wind up there will have the feathers off you if you let it.
And when it's done, come back down. I'll want to hear it from you.

speaker: nana
lines: Still here? Those batteries won't do much at the bottom of the hill, love.
Up through Windscar Ridge. Light the trail posts as you pass them.
Edda keeps the set at the mast on Brindle Peak. She's waiting on you.
Go on. I'm not going anywhere, and neither is the cabin.

speaker: nana
lines: A letter? From Pell, the postmaster, all the way across the valley?
'The blue house, road head.' Well, that's me. I painted it again in autumn, so there'd be no doubt.
Hm. I'll need to read that again. And again, probably.
This one stays by the stove. Tell Pell it found the right door, love. He frets.

speaker: nana
lines: There you are. I heard you on the radio. The whole valley did.

speaker: nana
lines: Edda says you did her looking for her. She sounded twenty winters younger.
Now. Tell me one thing. Just one, tonight. I'll have the rest out of you tomorrow.

choices.text: bram's pile is four hundred and eighty-one.
the sky went green over the peak.

speaker: nana
lines: I know. He told the whole valley on the radio. Then he told it again.
He'll count it tonight, twice. First night in years he'll like the answer.

speaker: nana
lines: The lights? Of course. Edda never could see the green. Now she knows it's there.
Was it as bright as they say? No, don't tell me. I'll picture it.

speaker: nana
lines: Sit out here with me a minute, then. I want to look at those posts.
The valley will be there in the morning. All of it. All of them.
And Pip. I'm glad it was you that went up.

speaker: nana
lines: Sit a minute and get warm. Whatever's out there will keep.
There's always a cup in this house for you. You know where they live.
Go on when you're ready. The valley's still yours to walk.

speaker: hollis
lines: You're Nana's. The one come up the road.
I've lost a mitten. The left one. The good one.
I know who took it. Fen, the owl who watches from the pines.
Go ask him. See what he says.

choices.text: why would fen take a mitten?

speaker: hollis
lines: He's an owl. He watches. He's got them big eyes.
And he never says anything. Guilty, if you ask me.
The pines. Creek side. That's where he sits.
Go on. Ask him.

speaker: hollis
lines: Ask him direct. Fen, the owl in the pines, won't volunteer a thing.
Drop a line in the creek pool below the split pine, too. In case he dropped it in, flying off.
Come back and tell me what he said.

speaker: hollis
lines: You fished it out of the creek? Below the split pine?
So it wasn't Fen. The wind. Huh.
I'll have to say something to him. Eventually.
Here. My spare. One mitten's no use to me. Don't argue, I don't want to owe you.

speaker: hollis
lines: The mitten's back on its hook, where it belongs.
I said sorry to Fen, the owl. Took me three tries. He nodded.
Wind's picking up. Keep your ears tucked in, Nana's girl.

speaker: hollis
lines: A headband? From Tamsin, the marten in the pines? For me?
...Tight round the ears. But it holds. And it's warm. Don't tell anyone I said warm.
Tell her it fits. And tell her she could have just asked me.

speaker: bram
lines: Four hundred and... no. That one's sticking out. Start again.
Batteries. Nana sent you. They're in the woodstore, behind that heap.
The end of the pile came down. No end, the rows lean, and I can't count a leaning row. Put it back and they're yours.

choices.text: why does it have to be straight?

speaker: bram
lines: A straight pile, you count the rows. A crooked one, you count every log. Three times today. Three numbers.
Can't go into winter with three numbers. Winter wants one.

speaker: bram
lines: Eight logs, square across each other. I'll know if you've cheated. I'll count.

speaker: bram
lines: Still a heap. I can see it from here.
Eight logs, square across each other. Then come and tell me.

speaker: bram
lines: Let me count. Four hundred and seventy-three in the rows. Eight on the end. Yours.
Four hundred and eighty-one. Twice running. Do you know how long it's been?
Here. The spare batteries. Mind them, they're the only ones in the valley.

speaker: bram
lines: And since you're going up: the bridge rope on Windscar Ridge is going. Everyone knows it.
Tuck, the marten who keeps that bridge, hasn't spoken to me in years. He won't come down and ask.
So take the good rope. Forty feet, coiled, no splices. I checked.
Tell Tuck I want it back the same length. I'll measure.

speaker: bram
lines: The rope's still in your bag? It's for Tuck, at the bridge on Windscar Ridge. It's on your way up.

speaker: bram
lines: It's tied? He took it? From me?
Still forty feet, he says. Come up and measure it, he says.
And what's that, bent at the bow? Give it here. That's my woodshed key.
I stood on it the winter we stopped talking. He's kept it tied in his rope all this time.
Well. Come spring I'll walk up there with my tape. Somebody has to check.

speaker: bram
lines: Four hundred and seventy-nine, eighty, eighty-one. Right. From the top. Don't talk, I'm counting.
Wood's the one thing in this valley that stays counted. I like that.
People don't. People keep changing their numbers.
Go on. Mind the pile on your way past.

speaker: edda
lines: A visitor, up here? You've climbed a long way to see a dead set.
I keep the radio at this mast. The whole valley talks through it.
Talked. It's dead for want of power. I'm waiting on batteries from below.
Nana Quill, at the cabin, is seeing to it. Tell her I'm still here.

speaker: edda
lines: You'll be Nana's Pip. I'd know that lantern anywhere. And those are my batteries.
There. Hear the hum? The set's warm. But it only reaches the valley when the aurora's up.

speaker: edda
lines: Here's my trouble. I'm an owl. I see the night in greys.
Three nights I've called on a bright cloud. Orla, Skiff, Wren, little Gus by his bell: nobody heard.
Nana's camera sees green. I don't.
Catch the aurora in a photograph, and tell me the moment it's up.

speaker: edda
lines: North, over the shoulder of the peak. It starts low, like a stain. Let it climb.
Then come straight to me. It doesn't stay long.

speaker: edda
lines: Then we wait another night. But the snow's coming, and the road shuts with it.
Look north, over the shoulder of the peak. Then come straight to me.

speaker: edda
lines: The set's warm and my talon's on the dial. The rest is the sky's.
North, over the shoulder of the peak. Green, low at first, then climbing. Get it on the camera, then tell me.

speaker: edda
lines: It's up? Then here we go. Stand by me.
Brindle Peak calling the valley. Brindle Peak calling. Anyone there? Over.
Nothing. Static. The sky has to find us first. Give it a...
There.

speaker: bram
lines: Hearth Hollow, by the big pine. Woodstore's full. Four hundred and eighty-one. Over.

speaker: orla
lines: Come and have some, any of you. Over.

speaker: skiff
lines: Boathouse on the Frozen Reach. The ice is holding. Lake's quiet. Over.

speaker: ivy
lines: Anyone cold, come down. Over.

speaker: wren
lines: Wren, in Pinewind Wood. The mast's humming again. I can hear it from here. Over.

speaker: gus
lines: Gus here, at the bell shop in the hamlet! I'm holding the big bell's rope!
Next time you call, I'll ring it. I will. Over.

speaker: edda
lines: Hear that, faint, under the rest? That's the road crew, below the pass.
They're bringing the plough up in the morning. The road stays open.

speaker: nana
lines: Edda, is that you? Is Pip up there with you?
Oh, good. That's good. Don't tell me anything. I want it from her.
And everyone along the trail: if there's a post near you, light it. She'll be coming down in the dark.

speaker: edda
lines: That's the valley, and the line holding.
Thirty winters I've kept this set. Never heard it so crowded.
Go on home, Pip. Follow the lights down.
I'll mind the set. Brindle Peak, over and out.

speaker: edda
lines: The line's holding. They've not stopped talking since.
Bram, down by the big pine, has read me his count four times.
Give Nana my love. She'll pretend she doesn't need it.
Mind the ridge on the way down. The wind's in a mood tonight.
